Apple has been working on AirPods with built-in cameras for some time, positioning visual intelligence features at the core of the product. The product was initially rumoured to launch this year, but was subsequently pushed back to sometime next year.

However, it now looks like we may see the first version of AirPods with a camera sometime this year. Here's why.

When news of AirPods with cameras first surfaced, there was talk of a single model: the codename B798. That model is still scheduled to arrive in 2027, and is expected to be the more advanced version.

But there's another model known as B790, and this version could be launching later this year. From the Power On newsletter:

For years, Apple has been working on AirPods with cameras under the codename B798. I previously reported that the device was originally planned to launch in 2026, and was then delayed to 2027. But Apple has also been working on another version under the codename B790 (as is well known, internally Apple develops competing versions of the same product).

This isn't the first time we've heard about the B790 version. Just last month, developer Sam Henri Gold spotted references to it in iOS 27 beta 2.

Only time will tell what these products ultimately look like, but there's a good chance that as early as September, we'll see the first version of AirPods with a camera. The differences between the B790 and B798 versions remain unclear, and it's also unclear whether both versions will ultimately make it to market.

Previous reports have pointed out that the stem of AirPods with cameras will be slightly longer than that of AirPods Pro, to accommodate the camera components, and will feature an LED indicator that lights up when data is being transmitted to the cloud.
